title: Auditing the impact of social media's policy shift on anti-vaccine discourse: A large language model-driven empirical study
summary: GPT-4o-assisted annotation of 13,458 COVID-19 vaccine-related tweets enabled a short-window analysis of discourse around X ending its misinformation policy. Anti-vaccine tweets increased after the policy change (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.50–1.72), largely through retweets; health-concern themes rose while conspiracy and anti-mandate shares declined. The 14-day observational pre/post comparison does not establish causation or long-term effects.
ai_technology: GPT-4o classified tweet stance, assigned anti-vaccine themes, and assessed stance consistency; the validated labels enabled analysis of changes in discourse patterns.
organization: Faculty of Applied Sciences, Macao Polytechnic University, Macao SAR, China; Beijing Key Laboratory of Mental Disorders, National Clinical Research Center for Mental Disorders & National Center for Mental Disorders, Beijing Anding Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China; Advanced Innovation Center for Human Brain Protection, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China; School of Computing Technologies, RMIT University, Melbourne, Australia

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: The paper reported external CAVES benchmark F1 of 0.883 for anti-vaccine stance and agreement checks, then analyzed a 14-day pre/post tweet sample.
evidence.unknown: Short observational pre/post window cannot isolate the platform policy as the cause or support conclusions about long-term discourse.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4o classified tweet stance, assigned anti-vaccine themes, and assessed stance consistency; the validated labels enabled analysis of changes in discourse patterns.
